zones.notes: Drop cloth runners at base of wainscot work area. Wainscot is low to floor — drips from brush/spray and sanding dust are the primary concerns. Standard edge protection.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to heavy_mask when wall above is SS_PAINTED_*
zones.notes: Paper masking above the wainscot cap rail line to protect finished wall field from overspray. Only needed for spray application. Brush application typically needs no wall masking.

protection_zones_analysis.conditional_protection_note: Floor protection is always required regardless of method. Wall masking is conditional on application_method = spray. Both zones use existing zone IDs — no new zones needed.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Wall field above wainscot meets at cap rail line. Different finish — wall paint (flat/eggshell) vs millwork enamel (satin/semi-gloss). Junction is at cap rail, which is handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT. No edge work from this spec — the cap rail provides the transition.

Cap rail at top of wainscot. Typically same color and sheen as wainscot panels. Cap rail handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT (ITM_TRIM_WAINSCOT_RAIL). Same finish group means no masking needed between them when painted in same session.

Standard baseboard below wainscot. Often same finish group. Baseboard handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT (ITM_TRIM_BASEBOARD). May be same or different color — when different, treated as separate finish group.
Wainscot meets door casing where both are present in the same wall. Complex intersection — wainscot panels terminate at casing edge. Typically same finish group.
Wainscot meets window casing where windows are within wainscot height zone. Complex intersection similar to door casing. Typically same finish group.

adjacency_analysis.surface_reference: Surface_Vocabulary_Reference.md v1.0 — wainscot_panel, wainscot_rail, wainscot_stile, wainscot_cap all exist in Millwork Surfaces section
adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Wainscot is typically part of the same finish group as surrounding trim (cap rail, baseboard, casings). Most adjacencies are same_finish relationships. The key different_finish adjacency is wall field above — separated by the cap rail. No edge work generated by this spec because transition surfaces (cap rail, baseboard) are separate specs.

affected_conditions.notes: Floor protection at wainscot base required when finished floors present. Subfloor requires no protection.

affected_conditions.modifier_notes: occupied_sensitive triggers OCC_SENSITIVE modifier 1.30x on protection tasks per Modifier_Registry
affected_conditions.notes: Additional protection when occupied. Rare in NC context but possible for renovation projects.
Temperature affects dry times, open time, and flow-out. Particularly impacts waterborne alkyd products at QT4+ which rely on extended open time for leveling.

MDF edge sealing uses solvent-based products (shellac/oil-based) — adequate ventilation required. Spray application generates overspray requiring air movement. Poor ventilation extends dry times for all coats.

valid_input_states.rationale: Combined prime+paint spec. SS_BARE (uncoated MDF, FJP, or solid wood wainscot) requires full primer coat — primer type driven by substrate. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY (standard NC — factory-primed MDF or FJP panels) skips primer, lighter prep.

output_state.rationale: Output state varies by sheen configuration dimension. Satin is default for wainscot (softer appearance on large panel areas).

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Typical NC: walls may be painted before wainscot (drywall painting before millwork detail). When walls SS_PAINTED_*: masking required above cap rail line during spray. When walls unfinished: no protection needed.
If cap rail already painted, mask top edge during wainscot spray. Typically same finish group — usually painted in same session, so rarely needs protection.
If baseboard already painted, mask during wainscot work. Same session painting typical.

required_paintscope_keys.description: Total SF of wainscot panel assembly below cap rail
required_paintscope_keys.catalog_status: PROPOSED — defined in Millwork Doctrine §1.1 but not yet in PaintScope catalog active entries

required_paintscope_keys.description: Floor protection area at wainscot work zone
Wall masking LF above wainscot cap rail line (spray only)

proposed_new_keys.description: Total SF of wainscot panel assembly below cap rail — includes panels, internal rails/stiles, base rail, and applied molding. Measured as wall area covered by wainscot system.
proposed_new_keys.justification: Defined in Millwork Doctrine §1.1 (Wainscoting: SF, PS_SURFACE_SF.WAINSCOTING) but not yet in PaintScope catalog active entries. Required as the primary input for this spec.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Wainscot meets wall field at cap rail line. The cap rail (SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT) provides the physical transition. No edge work from this spec — wall protection during spray is the only concern.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Typical NC: wall above may be at SS_BARE, SS_PRIMED_FIELD, or SS_PAINTED depending on sequence. Wall painting often precedes wainscot detail work.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Wainscot panel top edge meets cap rail bottom edge. Same finish group typical. Cap rail is trim spec scope. Panel-to-rail caulk joint included in this spec as prep task.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Cap rail and wainscot typically painted in same session with same material.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Wainscot base rail meets standard baseboard. Baseboard is trim spec scope. May be same or different finish group.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Baseboard installed after wainscot panels in typical NC sequence.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Internal edges within the wainscot assembly — panels meet internal rails and stiles. These are ALL within this spec's scope. Caulking at panel-to-frame joints is a mandatory prep task. Junction detail drives wainscot_type complexity modifier.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Internal assembly joints — all caulked during prep phase.

relevant_findings.topic: Single SF item for entire wainscot assembly
relevant_findings.finding: The wainscot assembly (panels, internal rails, stiles, base rail, applied molding) is measured as ONE item in SF. Internal framing complexity is captured by the wainscot_type modifier, not by splitting into separate LF and SF items. This matches Millwork Doctrine §1.1 which lists wainscoting as SF-based (PS_SURFACE_SF.WAINSCOTING).
relevant_findings.impact: Single ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL with SF UOM. All production rates expressed in SF/hr or hrs/SF.

relevant_findings.topic: Combined prime+paint spec — primer conditional on substrate_state
relevant_findings.finding: This spec includes both primer and finish coats, but primer is conditional. SS_BARE requires full primer coat (substrate-driven chemistry). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips primer — lighter prep only. Matches SF_WINDOW_INT_NC and SF_STAIR_RISER_NC pattern. Rationale: wainscot is a self-contained assembly with continuous surfaces that flow between components.
relevant_findings.impact: Module structure must support both workflows. Prime module is conditional. Two variant round configs: with/without primer.

relevant_findings.topic: Substrate drives primer chemistry — 5 distinct primer paths
relevant_findings.finding: MDF cut/routed edges: solvent-based sealer (Zinsser BIN Shellac, KILZ Original) — water-based causes irreversible fiber swelling. MDF faces: high-build latex (BM Enamel Underbody 217). FJP: stain-blocking primer MANDATORY (BM Prime Lock Plus). Solid wood softwood: standard primer-sealer (Zinsser Bulls Eye 1-2-3). Solid wood hardwood: tannin-blocking primer (BM Prime Lock Plus, SW Extreme Block). MDF requires TWO-STEP prime: edge seal (solvent) then face prime (latex).
relevant_findings.impact: Materials Manager must include 5 substrate-driven primer systems. SOP must have substrate-conditional primer tasks. MDF edge sealing is a separate mandatory task before latex primer.

relevant_findings.topic: Wainscot type drives complexity modifier per Millwork Doctrine §7.2
relevant_findings.finding: Three wainscot types with distinct production rate modifiers: flat_panel (1.0× — standard flat panels with simple frame), raised_panel (1.25× — 3D panel faces with detail edges, more cutting-in), beadboard (1.15× — uniform vertical grooves requiring additional attention). These map to Millwork Doctrine §7.2 complexity categories: flat_panel=simple profile (but not 0.85× because wainscot has internal framing), raised_panel=complex profile (1.25×), beadboard between standard and complex.
relevant_findings.impact: wainscot_type is a configuration dimension driving production rate complexity modifier. Applied to all qt_scaled tasks.

relevant_findings.topic: Cap rail exclusion — separate trim spec scope
relevant_findings.finding: The cap rail (wainscot top rail) is explicitly EXCLUDED from this spec. It is handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PRIME and SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT as ITM_TRIM_WAINSCOT_RAIL (LF-based, PS_SURFACE_LF.TRIM_WAINSCOT_RAIL). The cap rail is trim; the panel system below it is millwork. Same scope boundary logic as door casing (trim) vs door slab (separate spec).
relevant_findings.impact: No cap rail tasks in SOP. Caulk at wainscot-to-cap-rail junction IS included (prep task). Wall masking above cap rail line IS included (protection task for spray).

relevant_findings.topic: MDF edge sealing is a non-negotiable two-step process
relevant_findings.finding: When substrate is MDF and substrate_state is SS_BARE, the SOP MUST include solvent-based edge sealing as a separate prep task BEFORE latex face primer. Water-based primer on raw MDF edges causes irreversible fiber swelling. This is the same constraint as in SF_STAIR_RISER_NC — it is task-sequence critical, not just material selection.
relevant_findings.impact: SOP must enforce edge seal before face prime for bare MDF. Two separate tasks in prime module.

relevant_findings.topic: QT2 not applicable — wainscot is prominent millwork
relevant_findings.finding: Per Millwork Doctrine §6 and Fine Finish Doctrine: wainscot is a prominent, scrutinized surface. QT2 is not applicable. Minimum quality tier is QT3. This is consistent with all millwork/fine finish specs.
relevant_findings.impact: Spec configuration_dimensions must exclude QT2. Only QT3, QT4, QT5 valid.

relevant_findings.topic: Finish material systems — reuse existing SYS_FF_ IDs
relevant_findings.finding: Same SYS_FF_ finish systems as SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT, SF_WINDOW_INT_NC, and SF_STAIR_RISER_NC. QT3: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (100% acrylic enamel). QT4: SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (waterborne alkyd). QT5: SYS_FF_PREMIUM (premium urethane enamel). Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).
relevant_findings.impact: Reuse existing SYS_FF_ IDs. No new finish systems needed.

relevant_findings.topic: Interstage is universal at ALL quality tiers
relevant_findings.finding: Same pattern as all fine finish specs. Interstage runs after every coat except the final coat. Sanding discipline: QT3=spot sand only (nibs, rough spots), QT4=full 220 grit, QT5=thorough 220-320 grit. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD §15.4.1).
relevant_findings.impact: Interstage module present at all QTs. Sanding discipline varies by QT.

relevant_findings.topic: H1 height for all wainscot tasks — always below waist height
relevant_findings.finding: Standard wainscot is 32-42 inches tall. All work performed standing or kneeling. No access equipment required. Always H1 (1.0× modifier). Full-height paneling (floor-to-ceiling) is a separate future spec (SF_WOOD_WALL_NC).
relevant_findings.impact: No height dimension needed. All tasks use H1 modifier (1.0×).

relevant_findings.topic: Spray technique for wainscot — large panels spray efficiently
relevant_findings.finding: Wainscot panels have large flat areas that spray efficiently. Key challenge is detail at panel-to-frame junctions and frame profiles. Spray technique: field panels first (broad passes), then HVLP or fine-finish tip for frame detail. Backroll optional on flat panels for texture management. When spraying, wall above must be masked at cap rail line.
relevant_findings.impact: Spray is default application method for NC production. Backroll is optional (not coupled like wall spray). Wall masking is a spray-conditional protection task.

relevant_findings.topic: Caulking at three joint types within assembly
relevant_findings.finding: Wainscot prep includes caulking at: (1) panel-to-rail joints (horizontal internal joints), (2) panel-to-stile joints (vertical internal joints), (3) wainscot-to-wall junction (assembly perimeter where it meets drywall). All joints use paintable acrylic latex caulk. Caulk quantity derived from assembly SF — internal joint density varies by wainscot_type.
relevant_findings.impact: Three caulk task types in prep. Internal joint caulking is more intensive for raised_panel (more joints) and beadboard (groove-to-frame joints).

condition_drivers.notes: QT drives finish material system (recommendations), sheen restrictions, sanding between coats, inspection scrutiny. Does NOT drive primer selection (substrate-driven). Does NOT affect application quality baseline.
Spray is default for NC production — large flat panels spray efficiently. Brush for occupied spaces, small areas, or touch-up. Spray requires wall_adjacent masking. Per FFD §15.1.1.
flat_panel=1.0× (standard), raised_panel=1.25× (complex 3D profile), beadboard=1.15× (groove detail). Modifiers from Millwork Doctrine §7.2 complexity categories.
SS_BARE: full primer coat required (substrate-driven chemistry), heavier prep. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: skip primer, scuff sand only. Standard NC delivery is factory-primed.
Sheen/QT gate per FFD §4.1: satin at QT3+, semi-gloss at QT4+, gloss at QT5 only. Satin is default (softer appearance on wainscot panels).

quality_differences.qt3: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC — 100% acrylic enamel (ProClassic WB, Regal Select)
quality_differences.qt4: SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE — waterborne alkyd (BM Advance, SW Pro Industrial WB Alkyd)
quality_differences.qt5: SYS_FF_PREMIUM — premium urethane enamel (Emerald Urethane, Scuff-X)

quality_differences.qt3: Spot sand only — visible nibs, rough spots
quality_differences.qt4: Light full sand — 220 grit, entire surface for adhesion
quality_differences.qt5: Thorough full sand — 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern

quality_differences.qt3: Quick glance at 6ft distance — obvious defects only
quality_differences.qt4: Systematic scan at 3ft — all visible defects marked
quality_differences.qt5: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance
2-3 finish coats (3+ typical for brush per FFD §15.10.3)

quality_differences.qt3: Same baseline — no drips, sags, holidays, lap marks (NOT tiered)
Fill obvious holes, functional caulk lines, light scuff sand
quality_differences.qt4: Fill all visible holes, smooth caulk lines, full sand 180-220
quality_differences.qt5: Fill every hole, perfect caulk, thorough sand 220+, uniform scratch

failure_modes.failure: MDF fiber swelling on cut/routed edges
failure_modes.cause: Applying water-based primer to raw MDF cut/routed edges before solvent-based sealer
failure_modes.prevention: ALWAYS seal MDF edges with shellac-based (Zinsser BIN) or oil-based (KILZ Original) sealer FIRST. Two-step prime process for bare MDF. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine §2.1 and §4.1.
failure_modes.reversibility: Difficult — requires sanding back to substrate, fiber swelling is irreversible without aggressive sanding

failure_modes.cause: Using non-stain-blocking primer on bare finger-joint pine
failure_modes.prevention: ALWAYS use stain-blocking primer on bare FJP. BM Prime Lock Plus, BM Fresh Start oil-based, or Zinsser BIN Shellac. MANDATORY per Millwork Doctrine §2.2 and §4.1.
failure_modes.reversibility: Difficult — resin bleed re-emerges through multiple finish coats. Requires shellac-based primer to permanently block.

failure_modes.cause: Using water-based primer without tannin-blocking properties on bare hardwood (oak, maple, cherry)
failure_modes.prevention: ALWAYS use tannin-blocking primer on bare hardwood. BM Prime Lock Plus, SW Extreme Block, or shellac-based primer.
failure_modes.reversibility: Difficult — tannin bleed re-emerges through multiple finish coats. Requires stripping to bare wood and proper tannin-blocking primer.

failure_modes.cause: Incomplete coverage in raised panel profiles — brush/spray misses recessed areas at panel-to-frame transitions
failure_modes.prevention: Spray technique: field panels first, then HVLP for frame detail. Brush technique: work panel-to-frame sequence. Check all recessed profiles for holidays before moving on.
failure_modes.reversibility: Easy — additional coat addresses holidays. Part of interstage inspection.

failure_modes.cause: Excessive paint buildup in beadboard grooves, losing groove definition
failure_modes.prevention: Thin coats on beadboard. Spray preferred — atomized application minimizes groove fill. If brushing, use brush sized to groove width. Avoid over-application.
failure_modes.reversibility: Moderate — requires careful sanding in grooves to restore definition, then recoat.

failure_modes.failure: Brush marks on large flat panel areas
failure_modes.cause: Overworking waterborne product on large flat surfaces, inadequate open time management
failure_modes.prevention: Waterborne philosophy (FFD §15.3.1): Apply, tip once, walk away. Use quality brush with proper loading. Roll and Tip methodology (FFD §15.6) on flat panels. Sand out marks between coats with rigid block.
failure_modes.reversibility: Addressable — sand between coats with rigid block and recoat

failure_modes.cause: Wood movement and seasonal expansion/contraction in wainscot assembly, especially raised panels which move more than flat panels
failure_modes.prevention: Use quality paintable acrylic latex caulk. Apply after primer cure when possible. Proper joint width. Raised panel systems may experience more movement — use flexible caulk.
failure_modes.reversibility: Easy — re-caulk and touch-up. Part of maintenance.

failure_modes.cause: Differential movement between wood wainscot assembly and drywall wall, settling
failure_modes.prevention: Caulk at wainscot-to-wall junction. Flexible caulk accommodates movement. Standard NC prep task.

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: Dual material system — substrate-driven primer, QT-driven finish
notes_for_materials_manager.content: This spec has TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven (MDF edge seal + face prime, FJP stain-blocking, hardwood tannin-blocking, softwood standard). (2) Finish systems are QT-driven (SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, SYS_FF_PREMIUM). Same pattern as SF_STAIR_RISER_NC and SF_WINDOW_INT_NC.

MDF cut/routed edges: Solvent-based sealer (Zinsser BIN Shellac, KILZ Original). MDF factory faces: High-build latex (BM Enamel Underbody 217, ProClassic Undercoater). FJP: Stain-blocking primer MANDATORY (BM Prime Lock Plus, BM Fresh Start oil-based). Softwood: Standard primer-sealer (Zinsser Bulls Eye 1-2-3, KILZ 2). Hardwood: Tannin-blocking primer (BM Prime Lock Plus, SW Extreme Block). Factory-primed: No primer needed.

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: Finish material systems — reuse from trim/riser spec
notes_for_materials_manager.content: Same SYS_FF_ finish systems as all other fine finish specs. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

Paintable acrylic latex caulk for: (1) panel-to-rail joints (internal horizontal joints), (2) panel-to-stile joints (internal vertical joints), (3) wainscot-to-wall junction (assembly perimeter). Caulk quantity derived from assembly SF — internal joint density varies by wainscot_type.

Wainscot is measured directly in SF. Typical coverage: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth surface. Raised panel may consume ~10% more material due to increased surface area from 3D profile.

QT3: 220 grit for spot sanding only. QT4: 220 grit for full surface. QT5: 220-320 grit for full surface. Rigid sanding blocks mandatory for defect removal (FFD §15.4.1). Flexible sanding sponge acceptable for beadboard grooves and raised panel profiles.
Drop cloth runners at base of wainscot work area. Canvas drop cloths or builder's paper. Wainscot is low to floor — drip protection is primary concern.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Module structure is combined prime+paint with single SF UOM
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: SETUP → PREP → [PRIME (conditional)] → FINISH_COAT_1 → INTERSTAGE → FINISH_COAT_2 → [INTERSTAGE → FINISH_COAT_3 at QT5 brush] → FINAL_INSPECT → CLEANUP. Prime module runs only when substrate_state = SS_BARE. Factory-primed substrates skip from prep to finish.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: No canonical painting sequence — single paintable item
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: Unlike SF_STAIR_RISER_NC (stringers before risers) or SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC (balusters/newels/handrails), wainscot has only ONE paintable item (ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL, SF). No component-level sequencing required. Spray technique within the assembly: field panels first, then frame detail.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Prep tasks vary by substrate type
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: Bare MDF: sand faces 220, clean dust, fill fastener holes, caulk joints, MDF edge seal (separate mandatory task). Bare FJP: light sand 150-180, clean, fill, caulk. Bare softwood: sand 150-180, clean, fill, caulk. Bare hardwood: sand 150-220, clean, fill, caulk. Factory-primed: scuff sand 150-180, clean, fill, caulk.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Three caulk joint types in prep
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: (1) Panel-to-rail joints (horizontal internal), (2) panel-to-stile joints (vertical internal), (3) wainscot-to-wall junction (perimeter). All use paintable acrylic latex caulk. Caulk after fill and sand, before primer.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: MDF edge sealing is a separate mandatory task
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: For bare MDF: edge seal (solvent-based) MUST run BEFORE latex primer. Two-step prime: (1) TSK_WNSC_SEAL_MDF_EDGES, (2) TSK_WNSC_PRIME_FACES. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber swelling on MDF edges.

All task IDs use the WNSC context prefix per brief. Examples: TSK_WNSC_FLOOR_PROTECT, TSK_WNSC_WALL_MASK, TSK_WNSC_DUST_CLEAN, TSK_WNSC_SAND_PREP, TSK_WNSC_FILL_FASTENERS, TSK_WNSC_CAULK_JOINTS, TSK_WNSC_SEAL_MDF_EDGES, TSK_WNSC_PRIME_FACES, TSK_WNSC_FINISH_COAT, TSK_WNSC_INTERSTAGE_SAND, TSK_WNSC_FINAL_INSPECT.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Interstage is universal at ALL quality tiers
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: Interstage runs after every coat except the final coat. Tasks: clean area, inspect coat, sand (spot or full per QT), patch/repair defects, sand patches, spot coat. Scrutiny level is qt_scaled.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Wall masking is spray-conditional setup task
notes_for_sop_librarian.content: When application_method=spray: paper masking above cap rail line to protect wall field from overspray. Binary task — same at all QTs. Only applies to spray method.
At QT5 with brush application (especially semi-gloss/gloss), 3+ coats may be needed per FFD §15.10.3. Add additional FINISH_COAT + INTERSTAGE cycle as variant.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.content: All tasks use SF as the primary UOM. Production rates expressed in SF/hr. Wainscot SF directly from PaintScope input — no conversion needed.

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Production rate estimates from brief and doctrine
notes_for_estimation_engineer.content: Brief Section 13 provides rate guidance: Spray finish coat ~150-200 SF/hr (flat panel, QT3). Brush finish coat ~60-80 SF/hr (flat panel, QT3). QT4 multiplier ~0.80× on qt_scaled tasks. QT5 multiplier ~0.60× on qt_scaled tasks. These derive from Millwork Doctrine §7.1 trim rates adapted for panel SF.
flat_panel=1.0× baseline, raised_panel=1.25× (complex 3D profile), beadboard=1.15× (groove detail). Apply to all qt_scaled tasks. Modifiers from Millwork Doctrine §7.2.
Standard wainscot is 32-42 inches tall. Always H1 (1.0×). No access equipment needed. All work performed standing or kneeling.
QT3=1.00, QT4=1.30, QT5=1.50. Apply to inspection, repair, and sanding tasks. Do NOT apply to application rate — application quality is the same at all tiers.
Spray is significantly faster than brush on large flat panel areas (~2-3× for flat panels). The gap narrows for raised panel and beadboard where detail work is required regardless of method.

inherited_research_corrections.title: Do not specify dry times in specs
inherited_research_corrections.impact: No dry time references in materials or sop_modules — refer to PDS

inherited_research_corrections.title: Material systems are recommendations, not mandates
inherited_research_corrections.impact: Finish material systems are QT-driven recommendations — contractor has discretion

inherited_research_corrections.title: Advance is waterborne alkyd; Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel

assumptions.value: Spray finish coat ~150-200 SF/hr for flat_panel at QT3
assumptions.source: Brief Section 13 — derived from trim rates and panel SF adaptation
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides wainscot-specific SF production rates. Brief provides estimated ranges derived from trim LF rates. Field validation recommended.

assumptions.value: Brush finish coat ~60-80 SF/hr for flat_panel at QT3
assumptions.source: Brief Section 13 — derived from trim rates
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides wainscot-specific brush SF rates. Estimates reasonable given trim brush rates of 80 LF/hr (Millwork Doctrine §7.1).
Millwork Doctrine §7.2 has standard (1.0×) and complex (1.25×) modifiers. Beadboard at 1.15× is between these two categories — not explicitly in doctrine. Reasonable interpolation.

assumptions.value: Internal caulk joints per SF varies by wainscot_type — more joints in raised_panel than flat_panel
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical wainscot construction
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines internal joint density for wainscot types. Caulk consumption should be estimated per assembly, not per SF.

uncertainties.description: Millwork Doctrine §1.1 defines PS_SURFACE_SF.WAINSCOTING as the PaintScope key for wainscot measurement, but the key may not yet be active in the PaintScope catalog. Proposed as new key.
uncertainties.current_approach: Proposed as new key in proposed_new_keys. Proceeding with assumption it will be activated.

uncertainties.description: Brief sets QT3 default and satin default. These are compatible (satin at QT3+ per FFD §4.1). No tension exists — unlike stair riser spec where semi-gloss default conflicted with QT3 default.
uncertainties.current_approach: No issue — QT3+satin is a valid combination. No runtime gate rejection.

uncertainties.description: Raised panels have more surface area than flat panels due to 3D profile. Actual increase depends on profile depth and complexity. Estimated ~10% more material consumption.
uncertainties.current_approach: Flagged for Materials Manager to factor into coverage rates.
